stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to ~60,000 workers, about 27% of its staff, amid AI spending

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, Microsoft announced a Voluntary Exit Offer for certain employees in the US, Canada, India and the UK at level 70 and below; about 60,000 people are eligible.
key_facts.excerpt: The software maker announced a new voluntary exit offer for certain workers in the U.S., Canada, India and the United Kingdom at its experience level of 70 or below. Around 60,000 people are eligible

key_facts.fact: The eligible pool is about 27% of Microsoft's total workforce of 223,000 people.
key_facts.excerpt: The effort affects about 27% of Microsoft's total workforce of 223,000 people.

key_facts.fact: Employees must decide in early December, and those taking the offer will leave on Dec. 31.
key_facts.excerpt: Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31

key_facts.fact: Eligible units reportedly include AI experiences, Copilot, finance, HR, Xbox and Windows + Devices; marketing, commercial business and security are excluded.
key_facts.excerpt: including those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices... Units such as marketing, commercial business and security will be excluded

key_facts.fact: Microsoft has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for calendar 2026 and reports quarterly results after the close on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, slated to report first-quarter results after markets close Wednesday, has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year.

key_facts.fact: Earlier in 2026 Microsoft ran a voluntary retirement program for about 7% of its US workforce (~9,000 people) and in July cut 4,800 jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: The company earlier this year offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its U.S. workforce, or about 9,000 employees. In July, Microsoft announced it would cut 4,800 jobs

key_facts.fact: WSJ reported it is the largest voluntary buyout offer in Microsoft's history.
key_facts.excerpt: At Microsoft, it was the largest voluntary buyout offer in its history, extended to about one quarter of its staff, or 60,000 people.

stories.headline: Israel votes in first election since Oct. 7 with highest turnout since 1973; Netanyahu vs Eisenkot

key_facts.fact: Israelis voted on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, in the first nationwide election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: Israelis are voting today in the first nationwide election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023

key_facts.fact: Turnout reached 44.9% by 2 p.m. local time, the highest at that hour since 1973, per the Central Elections Committee.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 2 p.m. local time (8 a.m. ET), turnout in the election stands at 44.9%, according to Israel's Central Elections Committee, the highest turnout recorded at this hour since 1973.

key_facts.fact: Polling suggests a tight race between Netanyahu's Likud and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party.
key_facts.excerpt: Polling suggests a tight race between Netanyahu, leader of the nationalist Likud party, and his chief rival, Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar

key_facts.fact: An unprecedented 70,000 people reportedly flew home from abroad to vote; exit polls are due at 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT).
key_facts.excerpt: An unprecedented 70,000 people have reportedly flown home from abroad to vote... At 22:00 (20:00 GMT) on Tuesday, Israeli broadcasters will publish exit polls.

key_facts.fact: Many soldiers' and reservists' votes will not begin to be counted until Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: many of those votes will not begin being counted until Wednesday

key_facts.fact: No party has ever won a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, so coalition talks are expected to take weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: No single party has ever earned a majority in the Knesset... Negotiations to build a governing coalition will likely need to take place in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Egypt authorizes military support for Saudi Arabia; Iran says tanker hit mines east of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Oct. 26, Egypt's parliament voted to authorize President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: Egypt's parliament on Monday voted to authorize President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi to provide Saudi Arabia with military support in defending the kingdom against attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

key_facts.fact: The mandate passed with a two-thirds majority after three secret sessions and two postponements; the Social Democratic Party (11 seats) abstained.
key_facts.excerpt: The House of Representatives voted with a two-thirds majority... had held three rare secret meetings on the matter and postponed the vote twice... The Social Democratic Party, which holds 11 seats in parliament, abstained

key_facts.fact: Air defense systems and aircraft are expected but no ground troops; Sisi said support would defend Saudi territory and not include an attack on Yemen.
key_facts.excerpt: with air defense systems and aircraft expected but no ground troops

key_facts.fact: Iran's navy said on Oct. 27 an oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the vessel had switched off tracking and entered a restricted area.
key_facts.excerpt: the Navy said the tanker had switched off its tracking systems and was attempting to pass through a "restricted and unsafe" area when it hit the mines.

key_facts.fact: Iran's navy said the Strait of Hormuz remains "unsafe and closed" to vessels that do not coordinate passage with its armed forces.
key_facts.excerpt: It said the Strait of Hormuz remained "unsafe and closed" to vessels attempting to pass through without coordination.

key_facts.fact: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted talks with Qatar's emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at a Moscow gas summit on Oct. 27.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin is hosting talks with Qatar's emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the Moscow gas summit.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell 1.3% to $114.28 a barrel on Tuesday on the regional diplomatic push.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, were down 1.3% to $114.28 a barrel

stories.headline: Russia hits Kyiv with 16 ballistic missiles as Finland, Norway leaders hold rare call with Putin

key_facts.fact: Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones at Ukraine overnight, including a strike on Kyiv's South Bridge; Zelenskyy called it a serious escalation against logistics.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials in Kyiv said the South Bridge was hit in overnight attacks on the city that included 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones... "This is a serious escalation in Russia's campaign targeting our logistics," he said.

key_facts.fact: Russian ballistic missiles struck a university campus in Kyiv late Monday, killing one person; attacks in Kharkiv killed two.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian ballistic missiles damaged the grounds of a university in Kyiv, killing one person and leaving 10 injured... In Kharkiv... attacks late Monday killed two people and injured four.

key_facts.fact: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Store called Putin from Helsinki on Oct. 27 to convey messages ahead of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi in early November, then spoke with Zelenskyy.
key_facts.excerpt: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store called Putin from Helsinki on Tuesday to convey messages on future negotiations ahead of the Abu Dhabi meetings

key_facts.fact: Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since the 2022 full-scale invasion; the two leaders said they spoke for their own countries, not Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Both leaders said they spoke for their own countries, not Europe... Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion

key_facts.fact: A localized ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky took effect at 3 a.m. local time on Oct. 27, due to last until Saturday, to allow aid in; both sides confirmed it began.
key_facts.excerpt: The local ceasefire, due to last until Saturday in Russia-occupied Oleshky near the Crimean Peninsula, began at 3:00 a.m. local time to permit humanitarian aid to reach the city's inhabitants

key_facts.fact: Up to 2,000 people remain stranded in Oleshky, according to the UN.
key_facts.excerpt: Up to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky. They have been unable to leave because of explosive mines and drone attacks in the area, according to the United Nations.

stories.headline: DoorDash in advanced talks to buy Instacart for about $17 billion

key_facts.fact: DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart, in a deal that could be finalized as soon as this week and value Instacart at around $17 billion, WSJ reported on Oct. 26.
key_facts.excerpt: A deal could be finalized as soon as this week and could value Instacart at around $17 billion, the people said. There are no guarantees it will come together.

key_facts.fact: Instacart parent Maplebear rose 7.9% to close at $60.88 on Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: Maplebear rose 7.9% to close at $60.88 in New York trading Monday

key_facts.fact: Instacart had a market value of about $13 billion at Friday's close; DoorDash stock fell about 6% Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: Instacart was valued by the market at roughly $13 billion when trading ended on Friday. Instacart stock gained roughly 8% during Monday's regular session, whereas DoorDash stock slid roughly 6%.

key_facts.fact: Instacart's discussions with Uber over a transaction are dormant, according to Reuters; an announcement could come as early as Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Timing could be as early as Wednesday, according to Reuters... Instacart's discussions with Uber $UBER over a transaction are currently dormant, according to Reuters.

key_facts.fact: DoorDash is also buying Deliveroo as delivery companies push into groceries and retail.
key_facts.excerpt: DoorDash is buying Deliveroo, and Uber has acquired Postmates and Delivery Hero, according to Reuters.

stories.headline: US judge blocks Pentagon ban on contractors tied to Alibaba's lobbyists

key_facts.fact: A federal judge in San Jose on Monday, Oct. 26, granted Alibaba a preliminary injunction barring the US government from denying Pentagon contracts to companies that do business with firms lobbying for Alibaba.
key_facts.excerpt: A US federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba sued in June after the Pentagon added it to its list of companies allegedly aiding China's military, alongside Baidu and BYD.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba sued the US government in June after the Pentagon added it to a list of companies allegedly aiding China's military, alongside internet search provider Baidu, EV maker BYD

key_facts.fact: Alibaba had fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the June listing, per a Reuters source.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the Pentagon action in June

key_facts.fact: The ruling does not remove Alibaba from the list; the designation restricts Pentagon contracts and, from 2027, purchases via third parties.
key_facts.excerpt: Monday's injunction does not remove Alibaba from the Pentagon list... restricts Pentagon contracts with listed companies and, from 2027, purchases of their products or services through third parties.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg framed the ruling as testing Washington's ability to curtail Chinese companies' activities.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. won a US court ruling in its challenge to a Department of Defense blacklist, testing Washington's ability to curtail Chinese companies' activities.

stories.headline: FDA approves Pfizer's Talzenna plus Xtandi for earlier-stage HRR-mutated metastatic prostate cancer

key_facts.fact: On Oct. 26, 2026, the FDA approved talazoparib (Talzenna, Pfizer) with enzalutamide for metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive or -sensitive prostate cancer with HRR gene mutations.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 26, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved talazoparib (Talzenna, Pfizer Inc.) in combination with enzalutamide for the treatment of adults with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer with homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene mutations

key_facts.fact: The approval rests on the Phase 3 TALAPRO-3 trial of 599 patients; the combination cut the risk of radiographic progression or death by 52% (HR 0.48).
key_facts.excerpt: TALAPRO-3... 599 patients... median rPFS not reached... and 45.8 months... in the placebo and enzalutamide arm (Hazard Ratio 0.48 [95% CI: 0.36, 0.65]; p<0.0001)

key_facts.fact: An estimated 77% of patients on the combination remained progression-free at three years, per Pfizer.
key_facts.excerpt: an estimated 77% of patients remained progression-free at three years

key_facts.fact: The label covers both BRCA and non-BRCA HRR mutations, moving the PARP inhibitor combination to an earlier line than its 2023 approval for castration-resistant disease.
key_facts.excerpt: including both BRCA and non-BRCA mutations... This approval makes TALZENNA, an oral poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP inhibitor), plus XTANDI... available in an earlier line

key_facts.fact: Anemia was the most common grade 3+ adverse event, in 51% of combination patients vs 3% of controls; overall survival data were immature.
key_facts.excerpt: The most common grade 3 or higher TEAE was anemia, reported by 51% in the TALZENNA plus XTANDI group and 3% in the control group.
